metadata.title: Anthropic’s Growth is Slowing: Is AI Capex Next? | The Weekly Wrap
metadata.transcript_type: Local MLX Whisper automatic transcription; no speaker diarization

transcript_hash_basis: Normalized source metadata records the underlying full transcript hash. All normalized segments were read.
summary: The October 30 wrap links weaker AI financing and several earnings disappointments to possible capex deceleration. Anthropic growth and compute ratios support a narrow slowdown observation, but the token-maxing cause is unproven. Microsoft identifies delayed capacity delivery and Amazon reports accelerating AWS growth, important counterweights to the bearish cycle inference. Eisman clarifies fixed-coupon versus new-debt cost and presents conditional 2027 power constraints.
assessment: Empirical premises and forecasts are assessed separately. Guest assertions are not Eisman forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal attribution remain unresolved.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman solo, quoting two viewers. A Doomberg promotional excerpt and sponsor message are excluded.
framework_points: Separate sequential growth from absolute growth.
Compare revenue with compute expense, but do not treat the ratio as a complete profit model.
Distinguish GAAP EPS from investment gains and adjusted measures.
Distinguish fixed coupon cash payments from market funding cost.
Separate capex delivery delays from end-demand weakness.
Treat viewer field reports as hypotheses requiring broader validation.
tools_and_charts: Anthropic quarterly revenue, compute expense and efficiency ratio table
transcript_cautions: Local MLX Whisper transcription has no speaker diarization and garbles names.
Introductory Doomberg audio is a promotional excerpt, not adopted as a new Eisman forecast.
Viewer Joseph and Wayne assertions are attributed separately.
materiality_note: Major investment theses are distinguished from supporting factual premises. No overall accuracy percentage is appropriate.

claims.claim: A secondary bond yield rising above its coupon does not immediately raise the cash interest payment on an existing fixed-rate bond.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Inspect the relevant original financial, operational or economic data and compare the claimed mechanism with competing explanations.
claims.reason: The conditional relationship follows from the explicit assumptions; it does not establish that those assumptions hold in observed markets.
claims.next_check: Recheck the original data and subsequent realized outcomes.

assumptions: Bond coupon and principal are contractually fixed.
No restructuring, floating-rate reset or covenant-induced change occurs.
evidence_basis.proof: The issuer pays the contracted coupon times face value regardless of the secondary price. Yield changes because the buyer's price and expected return change. This corrects the earlier shorthand that existing debt cost rose immediately.
